intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII (OI13) is caused by homozygous mutation in the BMP1 gene (112264) on chromosome 8p21.3.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII (OI13) is caused by homozygous mutation in the BMP1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we describe a mutation associated to severe AR-OI (OI type III) in an additional gene, BMP1, which extends further the list of genes that are mutated in this heterogeneous disorder.
checks.explanation: Paper shows homozygous BMP1 mutation causes AR-OI; OI13 designation is OMIM nomenclature.

checks.claim: The BMP1 gene is located on chromosome 8p21.3.
checks.evidence_quote: BMP1 and its longer isoform mammalian Tolloid protein (mTLD) are alternative spliced products of BMP1 (MIM# 112264), which is located on 8p21.3.

paragraphs.text: Osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII is an autosomal recessive form of OI (Martínez-Glez et al. (2012)). Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) showed that the causative BMP1 mutation in their family resulted in a BMP1/mTLD protein with deficient proteolytic activity toward the C-propeptide of type I procollagen. The disorder is characterized by recurrent fractures and bone fragility (Asharani et al. (2012)). Asharani et al. (2012) reported increased bone mineral density in their family, whereas the patients reported by Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) had decreased bone density.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII is an autosomal recessive form of osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that BMP1 is an additional gene mutated in AR-OI.
checks.explanation: Paper describes autosomal recessive OI due to BMP1.

checks.claim: The causative BMP1 mutation in the family studied by Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) resulted in a BMP1/mTLD protein with deficient proteolytic activity toward the C-propeptide of type I procollagen.
checks.evidence_quote: proving that the Phe249Leu mutation leads to a BMP1/mTLD protein with deficient PICP proteolytic activity.

checks.claim: Osteogenesis imperfecta type XIII is characterized by recurrent fractures and bone fragility.
checks.evidence_quote: a consanguineous family affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures
checks.explanation: The abstract and the title ('leading to bone fragility in humans') describe recurrent fractures and bone fragility.

checks.claim: The family with OI13 reported by Asharani et al. (2012) had increased bone mineral density.
checks.evidence_quote: a consanguineous family affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures

checks.claim: The patients with OI13 reported by Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) had decreased bone density.
checks.evidence_quote: serpentine thin tibiae and fibulae in addition to S-curve scoliosis of thoracic and lumbar spine with platyspondyly, and generalized decreased bone density
checks.explanation: Decreased bone density reported (plus osteoporosis on DEXA in both).

paragraphs.text: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) studied a consanguineous Egyptian family with 2 children diagnosed with severe autosomal recessive OI. The affected children had recurrent fractures. They had generalized decreased bone density, with borderline osteoporosis to osteoporosis on bone densitometry.

checks.claim: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) studied a consanguineous Egyptian family with 2 children diagnosed with severe autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we have studied a consanguineous Egyptian family with two children diagnosed with severe autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (AR-OI) and a large umbilical hernia.

checks.claim: The 2 affected children from the consanguineous Egyptian family with OI13 had recurrent fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: Recurrent fractures of both upper and lower limbs occurred with an average rate of 15/year.

checks.claim: The 2 affected children from the consanguineous Egyptian family with OI13 had generalized decreased bone density.
checks.evidence_quote: serpentine thin tibiae and fibulae in addition to S-curve scoliosis of thoracic and lumbar spine with platyspondyly, and generalized decreased bone density
checks.explanation: Generalized decreased bone density stated explicitly only for the proband; brother had osteoporosis on DEXA but 'generalized' not stated for him.

checks.claim: Bone densitometry in the 2 affected children from the consanguineous Egyptian family with OI13 showed borderline osteoporosis to osteoporosis.
checks.evidence_quote: Bone densitometry (DEXA) at 5 years revealed borderline osteoporosis at the spine (Z-score −1.63) and osteoporosis at the left femur (Z-score −2.75).
checks.explanation: Proband had borderline osteoporosis at hip and spine; brother borderline to osteoporosis.

paragraphs.text: Asharani et al. (2012) described a consanguineous family affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures.

checks.claim: Asharani et al. (2012) described a consanguineous family affected by increased bone mineral density.
checks.evidence_quote: a consanguineous family affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures

checks.claim: Affected members of the consanguineous family described by Asharani et al. (2012) had multiple recurrent fractures.
checks.evidence_quote: a consanguineous family affected by increased bone mineral density and multiple recurrent fractures

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of OI13 in the family reported by Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) fit autosomal recessive inheritance: the 2 affected children were homozygous for the BMP1 mutation, whereas the parents and the unaffected sibs tested carried it in the heterozygous state. The finding of a homozygous BMP1 mutation in a consanguineous family by Asharani et al. (2012) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of OI13 in the Egyptian family reported by Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) fit autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Segregation analysis of the mutation within the family showed the two affected children to be homozygous for the c.747C>G nucleotide change, while the normal sister (II-2) and brother (II-4) from whom DNA was available and the parents carried the mutation in the heterozygous state.

checks.claim: The 2 affected children in the Egyptian family reported by Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) were homozygous for the BMP1 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Segregation analysis of the mutation within the family showed the two affected children to be homozygous for the c.747C>G nucleotide change

checks.claim: The parents and the tested unaffected sibs in the Egyptian family reported by Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) were heterozygous for the BMP1 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: while the normal sister (II-2) and brother (II-4) from whom DNA was available and the parents carried the mutation in the heterozygous state.

checks.claim: The finding of a homozygous BMP1 mutation in a consanguineous family by Asharani et al. (2012) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: we found a homozygous causative BMP1 mutation, c.34G>C, in a consanguineous family
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a homozygous mutation in a consanguineous family but does not state the inheritance pattern. 'Autosomal recessive' is an inference.

paragraphs.text: In 2 affected children from a consanguineous Egyptian family with OI13, Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) identified a homozygous c.747C-G transversion in exon 6 of the BMP1 gene, resulting in a phe249-to-leu (F249L) substitution within the protease domain. Type I procollagen analysis in supernatants from cultured patient fibroblasts showed abnormal processing of the procollagen C-propeptide, and the authors concluded that the mutation caused a strong reduction of BMP1/mTLD proteolytic function.

checks.claim: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) studied 2 affected children with OI13 from a consanguineous family.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we have studied a consanguineous Egyptian family with two children diagnosed with severe autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (AR-OI)
checks.explanation: The paper describes two affected children with AR-OI from a consanguineous family. OI13 is OMIM's label for this disorder.

checks.claim: The consanguineous family with OI13 studied by Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) was Egyptian.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we have studied a consanguineous Egyptian family with two children diagnosed with severe autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta (AR-OI)
checks.explanation: The paper states that the family is Egyptian.

checks.claim: In 2 affected children from a consanguineous Egyptian family with OI13, a c.747C-G transversion in exon 6 of the BMP1 gene was identified.
checks.evidence_quote: found a homozygous c.747C>G nucleotide change in exon 6 that causes the substitution of phenylalanine at position 249 to leucine (p.Phe249Leu)
checks.explanation: The c.747C>G change is in exon 6 of BMP1, and a figure legend calls it a transversion.

checks.claim: The BMP1 c.747C-G variant was homozygous in the 2 affected children from the consanguineous Egyptian OI13 family.
checks.evidence_quote: Segregation analysis of the mutation within the family showed the two affected children to be homozygous for the c.747C>G nucleotide change
checks.explanation: Both affected children are homozygous for the variant.

checks.claim: The BMP1 c.747C-G transversion results in a phe249-to-leu (F249L) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: causes the substitution of phenylalanine at position 249 to leucine (p.Phe249Leu)
checks.explanation: p.Phe249Leu is the same substitution as phe249-to-leu (F249L).

checks.claim: The BMP1 F249L substitution lies within the protease domain.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis identified both patients with a Phe249Leu homozygous missense change within the BMP1 protease domain
checks.explanation: The paper places the residue in the BMP1 protease domain.

checks.claim: Type I procollagen analysis in supernatants from cultured fibroblasts of patients with the homozygous BMP1 F249L variant showed abnormal processing of the procollagen C-propeptide.
checks.evidence_quote: Type I procollagen analysis in supernatants from cultured fibroblasts demonstrated abnormal PICP processing in patient-derived cells
checks.explanation: PICP is the procollagen I C-terminal propeptide, so this matches abnormal C-propeptide processing.

checks.claim: Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) concluded that the BMP1 F249L mutation caused a strong reduction of BMP1/mTLD proteolytic function.
checks.evidence_quote: thus indicating that the Phe249Leu mutation causes strong reduction of the BMP1/mTLD proteolytic function and confirming the pathogenicity of the mutation
checks.explanation: The paper states this conclusion directly.

paragraphs.text: In a consanguineous family with OI13, Asharani et al. (2012) identified a homozygous c.34G-C mutation in the BMP1 gene. The mutation was located within the BMP1 signal peptide and led to impaired secretion and an alteration in posttranslational modification, consistent with reduced BMP1 function.

checks.claim: Asharani et al. (2012) identified a homozygous c.34G-C mutation in the BMP1 gene in a consanguineous family with OI13.
checks.evidence_quote: we found a homozygous causative BMP1 mutation, c.34G>C, in a consanguineous family
checks.explanation: The variant and zygosity match. The abstract does not use the label OI13.

checks.claim: The BMP1 c.34G-C mutation is located within the BMP1 signal peptide.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation is located within the BMP1 signal peptide

checks.claim: The BMP1 c.34G-C mutation led to impaired secretion of BMP1.
checks.evidence_quote: leads to impaired secretion and an alteration in posttranslational modification

checks.claim: The BMP1 c.34G-C mutation led to an alteration in posttranslational modification of BMP1.
checks.evidence_quote: leads to impaired secretion and an alteration in posttranslational modification

checks.claim: The effects of the BMP1 c.34G-C mutation were consistent with reduced BMP1 function.
checks.evidence_quote: Attenuated BMP1 function compromises osteogenesis, leading to bone fragility in humans and zebrafish.
checks.explanation: The title says BMP1 function is attenuated (reduced).

paragraphs.text: Asharani et al. (2012) characterized a zebrafish bone mutant harboring lesions in bmp1a. They found that Bmp1a is critically required for mature-collagen generation, downstream of osteoblast maturation, in bone, demonstrating conservation of BMP1 function in osteogenesis across species.

checks.evidence_quote: Bmp1a is critically required for mature-collagen generation, downstream of osteoblast maturation, in bone

checks.evidence_quote: Bmp1a is critically required for mature-collagen generation, downstream of osteoblast maturation, in bone

clinical_synopsis.feature: Increased bone mineral density (in one family)

paragraphs.text: In 2 affected children from a consanguineous Egyptian family with OI13, Martínez-Glez et al. (2012) identified a homozygous phe249-to-leu (F249L) mutation within the protease domain of the BMP1 gene. The patients had generalized decreased bone density. Functional studies showed that the mutation resulted in a BMP1/mTLD protein with deficient proteolytic activity toward the type I procollagen C-propeptide.

checks.evidence_quote: Mutation analysis identified both patients with a Phe249Leu homozygous missense change within the BMP1 protease domain

checks.evidence_quote: Phe249 is a residue contained within the peptidase domain of BMP1/mTLD

checks.explanation: Generalized decreased bone density stated explicitly only for the proband; brother had osteoporosis on DEXA.

checks.claim: Functional studies showed that the BMP1 F249L mutation resulted in a BMP1/mTLD protein with deficient proteolytic activity toward the type I procollagen C-propeptide.
checks.evidence_quote: proving that the Phe249Leu mutation leads to a BMP1/mTLD protein with deficient PICP proteolytic activity.

paragraphs.text: In a consanguineous family with OI13, Asharani et al. (2012) identified a homozygous c.34G-C mutation in the signal peptide of BMP1. Affected individuals had multiple fractures and increased bone mineral density. Functional studies showed that the mutation led to impaired secretion and an alteration in posttranslational modification, reducing BMP1 function.
